newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Diesel rebounds, fuel oil drifts.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Diesel rebounds, fuel oil drifts.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps at midday on Tuesday rebounded slightly after Monday's plunge but recovery is seen shortlived as the market remains choked with supplies, brokers said.
July gas oil swaps were quoted at $23.35/$23.45 per barrel, up between 5-10 cents from Monday's quotes. August was bid at $23.40.
"Levels improved slightly this morning...I think the crash was just too much yesterday, but sentiment is still bearish," said one trader.
"The recovery will be brief and with crude easing off by another 14 cents yesterday, the outlook remains gloomy," said another trader.
July Brent closed 14 cents down at $17.56 a barrel on Monday.
Traders said the cash market is flooded with supplies as majors suffering from brimming inventories were offering the market down.
A U.S major was offering as low as $23.00 for July barrels late Monday. The agressive offers caused gas oil cash quotes to fall by around $1.10 per barrel, ending at $23.00/$23.80 late Monday.
"Most traders long on supplies, are buying paper to cover their positions," said one trader, citing the active trade seen Monday.
Traders said Chinese demand has slowed down to a snail's pace.
"Just a small parcel of 10,000 tonnes was fixed yesterday," said the trader.
Traders said the physical market threatens to break support at $24.00 or even test the $23.00 mark later today.
Prompt physical gas oil has not traded below $24.00 since July last year.
Brokers said July jet/gas oil regrade was quoted at plus $0.20/0.35, from Monday's indications at $0.10/0.20 cents.
Traders attributed the widening regrade quotes to the weakness in the gas oil market.
Fuel oil swaps hovered around Monday's quotes. June swaps was last quoted at $99.00/$100.25 and July at $99.00/$100.25.
